title: No Eyebrows? 54% Can't Recognize You 🤨
description:
Why do we have eyebrows? Their outward-pointing hairs and arch steer sweat and rain off to the sides so it stays out of your eyes, and a 2003 MIT study found people recognized famous faces less often without eyebrows (46%) than without eyes (60%).

Sources:
https://www.healthline.com/health/why-do-we-have-eyebrows
https://www.mentalfloss.com/science/body/why-do-we-have-eyebrows
https://jaepakmd.com/resources/why-do-we-have-eyebrows/

Animated in the Kawaii Anime style.
pinned_comment: Can you raise just one eyebrow? Left, right, or neither? 🤨
script: Lose your eyebrows and 54% of people can't name your face. MIT scientists tested it in 2003. They showed people famous faces with the eyes erased, and they still named sixty percent. But erase just the eyebrows, and it dropped to forty-six. So why do we even have them? Picture sweat rolling down your forehead. Your brow bone and that arch catch it like a gutter, and the hairs all point out toward your ears, so the drops slide off to the sides, and not into your eyes. Rain too. Each brow has about 250 hairs on the job. But their biggest job? Talking without words. One brow up means, really? Both up means surprise! Pulled down and together? Somebody's grumpy. So can you raise just one eyebrow? Left, right, or neither?
key_facts: Eyebrow hairs grow outward toward the sides of the face, steering sweat and moisture away from the eyes (Healthline, Mental Floss)
In a 2003 MIT study (Sadr et al., Perception), famous faces were identified 60% of the time with eyes removed but only 46% with eyebrows removed (Healthline)
An average eyebrow has roughly 250 hairs (Jae Pak MD)
Eyebrows are key to expressions: one raised for skepticism, both raised for surprise, lowered for anger or concern (Healthline, Mental Floss)
